title: Normals and the front face
cards/0/title: A face has a front and a back
cards/0/body:
The order in which a triangle’s vertices are listed sets its front side. Counterclockwise (as you look at the triangle) means it faces you; clockwise means you see its back.

The GPU usually skips the back side, which saves almost half the work. This is called backface culling.
cards/1/task: Build the house so every triangle faces you (green). Got a red one? Reverse its winding.
cards/2/q: In a game, some faces of a model vanished: you can only see them from inside. Most likely…
cards/2/options/0: Those triangles have reversed winding, so their normals point inward
cards/2/explain: Back faces are culled, so flipped faces disappear from the outside. In an editor you fix it by recalculating normals to point outward.
cards/3/title: A normal is an arrow pointing out
cards/3/body:
A normal is a unit vector perpendicular to the surface. Lighting uses it: how much the surface is turned toward the light.

In STL each triangle has one normal. In OBJ and glTF normals are stored per vertex, which allows smooth lighting.
cards/3/deep: There are also normal maps: textures that replace the normal at every point and draw fine detail without extra triangles. To orient such a texture correctly you need tangents.
cards/4/task: Switch between flat and smooth normals and compare how many vertices the GPU needs.
cards/5/q: Why does the GPU need more vertices with flat normals?
cards/5/options/0: To the GPU a vertex is a position plus a normal; on an edge between faces with different normals, the point has to be stored twice
cards/5/options/2: It is a bug in the demo
cards/5/explain: The GPU cannot do “one point, two normals”. A sharp edge means duplicated vertices.
cards/6/q: A cube with sharp edges has 8 corners. How many vertices will the GPU get?
cards/6/explain: Each corner belongs to three faces with different normals, so it gets three copies: 8 × 3 = 24.
cards/7/options/0: The order of a triangle’s vertices sets its front side
cards/7/options/1: glTF treats counterclockwise winding as the front
cards/7/options/2: Normals are needed to compute lighting
cards/7/options/3: A normal is the color of a vertex
cards/7/options/4: The back of a triangle is always drawn
cards/7/explain: A normal is a direction, not a color. You can turn on back faces (a double-sided material), but by default they are culled.
